title: Risk-scored canary evacuation policy with multi-metric hysteresis and cost weighting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a risk-scored canary evacuation policy that automatically evicts traffic from a candidate model variant when a composite risk score (derived from latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput signals) exceeds a tunable band. The policy must be cohort-aware, account for cost sensitivity, and include hysteresis (patient detectors + decay) to avoid oscillation. It should support shadow traffic experiments, A/B comparisons, and an operator override UI in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Risk score computed as weighted aggregation of normalized signals (latency P95, error rate, tokens-per-request cost, throughput per GPU) and exposed as a single metric in Grafana
Evacuation action: automatic traffic ejection and fallback to stable model applied when risk score breaches an upper threshold for a sustained window (configurable)
Hysteresis: once evacuated, model must remain out of rotation until risk score decays below a lower threshold for N minutes (configurable) to prevent flip-flop
Cohort-aware baselining: scoring uses cohort baselines (region, customer tier, request size) and can be toggled to global baseline
Operator controls: Console toggle for enabling auto-evacuation per deployment, manual force-evacuate/reinstate buttons, and audit log entries for all actions
End-to-end tests that simulate noisy latency spikes vs sustained regressions and assert correct evacuation/restore behavior
Dashboard + alerting: Grafana dashboard tile and an alert rule that surfaces when risk score crosses warning and critical bands
decisions: Use a logistic transform on each raw signal to normalize disparate ranges before weighting (significant improvement in stable weighting during experiments)
Expose per-signal sensitivity knobs (weight and slope) rather than attempting to auto-learn weights in first iteration to accelerate rollout and safety reviews
Implement decay-based hysteresis (exponential decay with configurable half-life) rather than fixed time windows to better handle bursty workloads
Evacuation will perform a traffic replica-weight shift (gradual ejection over 30s) rather than hard cut to reduce downstream cascade risk
Store all evacuation decisions in existing rollout audit log (Console) and emit structured events to internal event bus for downstream analysis
updates: 2026-03-09: Spike experiment plan drafted and shared in #infra-rollouts. Decided to run initial metric normalization analysis against last 90 days of production traces (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412).

2026-03-10: Implemented prototype risk score function in Canary Controller (branch: feat/canary-risk-score). Local unit tests cover logistic transforms and weighted aggregation. Pending integration tests.

2026-03-11: Design review with PM + SRE. Major feedback: need cohort baselines for large enterprise customers to avoid noisy false positives during low-volume cohorts. Added cohort routing key to scoring pipeline.

2026-03-12: Benchmarked evacuation latency for gradual ejection vs hard cut across Dedicated pool. Observed 12% lower downstream tail latency with gradual ejection. Results in doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Risk+Score+Evacuation+Benchmark

2026-03-13: Opened RFC describing operator controls and fallback policies; linking GH RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/78. Assigned QA to create chaos tests that inject token-cost regressions from adversarial prompts.
2026-03-13: Blocker identified: need a small data-contract change in telemetry ingestion to include request_size_bucket; raised dependency on ENG-59902 (telemetry) and added to dependencies list.
Next steps: finish integration tests, add Grafana tiles, run canary in shadow mode against 5% traffic for two weeks, then pilot auto-evacuation on non-critical tenant group.
risks_mitigations: Risk: false positives in low-volume cohorts -> Mitigation: cohort-aware baselining + minimum sample threshold before auto-evacuation
Risk: downstream capacity shocks during evacuation -> Mitigation: gradual ejection, preflight capacity check, and automatic fallback to pinned stable variant
Risk: cost-driven oscillation when token-cost weight is high -> Mitigation: include cost deadband and decay-based lower threshold before re-admittance
Risk: operator confusion -> Mitigation: Console UX with clear state, timeline, and one-click manual override + audit trail
